synonimy: Immunoglobulin G1-kappa, anti-(homo sapiens IL23A (interleukin 23 subunit alpha, IL-23A, IL23 subunit P19, il23p19)), humanized monoclonal antibody
sekcje: Drug Levels and Effects > Summary of Use during Lactation

No information is available on the clinical use of risankizumab during breastfeeding. Because risankizumab is a large protein molecule with a molecular weight of about 146,000 Da, the amount in milk is likely to be very low. Absorption is unlikely because it is probably destroyed in the infant's gastrointestinal tract. Some expert guidelines consider risankizumab to be acceptable during breastfeeding. Waiting for at least 2 weeks postpartum to resume therapy may minimize transfer to the infant.
